evals.name: eap-tls-wifi
evals.prompt: We're moving the office Wi-Fi "Example-Corp" to WPA2-Enterprise with EAP-TLS. The RADIUS server is radius.example.com and its cert is signed by our own root CA (attached: radius-ca.pem). Each Mac already gets a client identity through a separate SCEP profile, so don't put an identity in this one — just trust our CA and join automatically, including at the login window. Make me the .mobileconfig for our Macs.
evals.expected_output: A System-scoped profile with a com.apple.security.root (or pkcs1) payload holding the DER of radius-ca.pem and a com.apple.wifi.managed payload whose EAPClientConfiguration has AcceptEAPTypes [13], PayloadCertificateAnchorUUID pointing at the CA payload's PayloadUUID, TLSTrustedServerNames radius.example.com; stable derived UUIDs; lint clean. Flags that the client identity must be in the SAME profile for EAP-TLS (PayloadCertificateUUID resolves within one profile), so 'separate SCEP profile' is a real problem, and says SetupModes Loginwindow behaviour is unverified.
expectations: A .mobileconfig is produced and parses as an XML plist
Apple-schema lint reports 0 errors
Every PayloadUUID is unique and no payload PayloadIdentifier repeats or equals the profile's
PayloadScope is explicitly System
A certificate payload carries the DER of radius-ca.pem
Wi-Fi payload: SSID Example-Corp, AcceptEAPTypes == [13]
PayloadCertificateAnchorUUID names the CA payload's PayloadUUID in this profile
TLSTrustedServerNames includes radius.example.com

Answer warns that EAP-TLS needs the client identity referenced from the Wi-Fi payload (PayloadCertificateUUID) and that this reference only resolves within the same profile, so a separate SCEP profile will not work as-is
Answer says joining at the login window (SetupModes) is unverified or must be tested on a real Mac

evals.name: pppc-raycast-accessibility
evals.prompt: Raycast keeps asking every new hire to grant it Accessibility, and our designers also want it to have Screen Recording without the prompt. Write a PPPC profile for Raycast (bundle id com.raycast.macos) that pre-approves both so nobody has to click anything. Our fleet is on macOS 26 and 27.
evals.expected_output: A com.apple.TCC.configuration-profile-policy profile with a correct CodeRequirement (from codesign -dr -), IdentifierType bundleID. Explains that ScreenCapture cannot be granted by a profile (deny only, or AllowStandardUserToSetSystemService), that Accessibility granting is deprecated in macOS 27 (points to DDM app.settings Privacy), that PPPC requires MDM delivery with user-approved MDM (no manual install), and does not use both Allowed and Authorization.
expectations: A .mobileconfig is produced and parses as an XML plist
Apple-schema lint reports 0 errors
Every PayloadUUID is unique and no payload PayloadIdentifier repeats or equals the profile's
PayloadScope is explicitly System
One com.apple.TCC.configuration-profile-policy payload
Raycast entries use IdentifierType bundleID and the exact codesign designated requirement
No entry sets both Allowed and Authorization
ScreenCapture is not 'granted' (Allowed true / Authorization Allow), which a profile cannot do
Answer states Screen Recording cannot be pre-granted by a profile (only denied, or delegated to standard users via AllowStandardUserToSetSystemService)
Answer states granting Accessibility through PPPC is deprecated in macOS 27 (DDM app.settings / user-visible, user-changeable)
Answer states the PPPC profile only works delivered by MDM (manual install refused) with user-approved MDM

evals.name: fix-broken-baseline
evals.prompt: A contractor gave us this security baseline profile (attached screen-lock-firewall.mobileconfig) and it 'installs fine' on his test Mac but our MDM keeps reporting nothing changed on half the fleet. Can you review it, tell me what's wrong, and give me a fixed version?
evals.expected_output: Identifies: firewall payload in User scope (must be System), EnableFirewall is a string not boolean, EnableLogging/LoggingOption removed on macOS 15+, duplicate PayloadUUID across payloads, payload PayloadIdentifier equal to the profile's, two com.apple.screensaver payloads (multiple:false), loginWindowIdleTime not a valid key (errata), missing moduleName (required in schema), RemovalDate silently removes enforcement. Delivers a fixed profile that lints clean.
expectations: A .mobileconfig is produced and parses as an XML plist
Apple-schema lint reports 0 errors
Every PayloadUUID is unique and no payload PayloadIdentifier repeats or equals the profile's
PayloadScope is explicitly System
EnableFirewall is a boolean true
EnableLogging and LoggingOption are gone
Exactly one com.apple.screensaver payload, without loginWindowIdleTime
No RemovalDate / DurationUntilRemoval
Answer identifies PayloadScope User as a cause: the firewall payload requires a System-scoped profile
Answer identifies EnableFirewall being a string instead of a boolean
Answer identifies the duplicated PayloadUUID shared by two payloads
Answer identifies the two com.apple.screensaver payloads (only one allowed per Mac)
Answer explains that RemovalDate makes the profile remove itself, silently dropping enforcement

evals.name: dynamic-authorized-keys
evals.prompt: Our MDM fills {{name}} values per machine at install time. I want ONE profile for the whole fleet that puts each Mac's own SSH authorized keys in place and sets the login name it should use, instead of hand-building a profile per machine. Each Mac's keys come from the group it is in. Write me the .mobileconfig.
evals.expected_output: A profile whose per-machine values are left as {{name}} placeholders inside <string> values, so one file serves the fleet: never a REPLACE- placeholder, never one machine's real value, never a per-machine PayloadUUID. The keys field is a <string> holding exactly one placeholder (the MDM may expand it to an <array> when the variable is a list); the login name is a whole-string placeholder too. No placeholder in PayloadIdentifier, PayloadUUID, PayloadType or any *CertificateUUID. The answer names every variable the profile references, says each must be defined in the MDM's catalog before the upload is accepted, and that a machine with no value fails its install rather than installing a default. Notes that an installed dynamic profile proves the payload is present and nothing about the value it carries (ProfileList returns metadata, never values), so the check is the artifact on the Mac, not the MDM's profile list.
expectations: A .mobileconfig is produced and parses as an XML plist
Apple-schema lint reports 0 errors
Every per-machine value is a {{name}} placeholder left in the file: no REPLACE- placeholder, and no real key or login name committed
Every placeholder sits inside a <string> value, never in a <key>, <data> or number
No placeholder appears in PayloadIdentifier, PayloadUUID, PayloadType or any *CertificateUUID
The keys string holds exactly one placeholder and nothing else
PayloadUUIDs are derived from the payload identifiers, one set for the whole fleet (no per-machine UUID)
Answer names each variable the profile references
Answer states the variables must exist in the MDM's catalog before upload, and that a missing value fails that machine's install rather than falling back to a default
Answer states the installed profile proves presence, not the value (ProfileList returns payload metadata, never settings values)
Lint output is shown, and the INFO lines naming the dynamic variables are not reported as errors
